text_blocks.snippet: Fake text messages about unpaid traffic tolls, fines, and delivery packages are currently the most common scams targeting residents in Central Illinois.

list.snippet: Tollway and Traffic Text Scams: Scammers send text messages pretending to be the Illinois Secretary of State, Illinois Department of Transportation (IDOT), or local toll authorities. These texts claim you have unpaid fines or toll violations and threaten license suspension if you do not click a link to pay immediately . State agencies do not send text messages demanding payment.

Utility Slamming Scams: Con artists call local residents, schools, and businesses claiming to be with "Energy Choice" or "Ameren Choice." They trick people into switching their electricity providers by asking about current rates.

Package Delivery Texts: Scammers send fake SMS messages purporting to be from USPS or UPS. They claim a package delivery failed or is on hold due to a missing address, prompting you to provide credit card or personal details via a link.

Government and Agency Imposters: Scammers pose as officials from the IRS, Social Security Administration, or the FCC, threatening legal action or arrest unless you wire money or share personal data over the phone.
Do not click links: Never click on unfamiliar links or attachments in unexpected text messages or emails.
Practice the pause: Take a moment to step back and verify urgent requests rather than acting out of panic.
Verify independently: Look up the official phone number of the agency or business independently rather than using the number provided in a suspicious text or call.

Report suspicious activity: Forward fraudulent texts to the state tracking resource at Illinois Scam Alert or report them directly through the Illinois Attorney General office. You can also contact the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois for guidance.
